text:
max (Support): Hi team — customer Jane at ACME says their long generation jobs keep getting cut off ~15s after the request despite setting long timeouts in our Python SDK. They hit a 504-like error and partial stream.
jane (Customer): reproducible with our prod proxy. We call `client.generate()` with timeout 300s. After ~15s stream stops, rest of tokens lost.
max (Support): Can you paste the minimal repro?
jane (Customer): Here's trimmed code: ```python
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=..., timeout=300)
r = c.responses.create(..., stream=True)
for chunk in r: print(chunk)
``` stream + timeout=300.
max (Support): Noted. They also run behind an internal HTTP proxy (env HTTP_PROXY set).
elaine (SRE): Quick theory: proxy/ALB has its own idle timeout around 15s and might close the socket; SDK's `timeout` may be treated as per-chunk read deadline rather than total deadline. :thinking_face:
nitin (SDK): Hmm, SDK changed semantics in v0.13 — `timeout` used to be total, now we accept either a number (per-IO) or a `Timeout` object. If they passed an int it's applied to socket read not the total request. Which SDK version?
jane (Customer): pip shows redwood-sdk==0.13.1 in their environment.
nitin (SDK): That explains it. In 0.13 we introduced streaming chunk timeouts to avoid hanging sockets; integer `timeout` maps to connect/read chunk timeout. For long generations you must pass `timeout=Timeout(total=300)` or `timeout={"total":300}`.
max (Support): Can you confirm behavior with HTTP_PROXY in path?
elaine (SRE): I reproduced locally: with HTTP_PROXY=our-proxy and `timeout=300` (int) the proxy's 15s idle closes the connection; SDK retries once then gives up, producing truncated stream.
max (Support): Any quick workaround for customers on 0.13?
nitin (SDK): Two options: 1) set timeout as a dict/Timeout object to express total deadline, e.g. `Timeout(total=300, connect=10)`; 2) bump proxy idle timeout or enable proxy keep-alives. Also recommended to upgrade to 0.13.2 where we emit clearer logs when proxy resets.
jane (Customer): Is there a way to avoid changing proxy configs? They can't.
nitin (SDK): Use streaming heartbeats: send ``keepalive: True`` isn't supported server-side, but you can use smaller `read_chunk` timeouts if you can tolerate intermittent flushes. Or set `timeout={"total":600, "read":30}` so total covers long job and read ensures each chunk tolerates 30s between chunks.
elaine (SRE): I posted a repro script in #eng-sre with curl vs sdk comparison. With curl: `curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." https://api.redwood.com/v1/responses/stream` and the proxy behaves similarly — so it's not purely SDK.
max (Support): Customer also reported different behavior on Linux vs macOS — maybe different HTTP libs (urllib3 vs httpx)?
nitin (SDK): Right — our Python SDK can use `requests` (urllib3) or `httpx` depending on env. The timeout semantics differ. On httpx, `timeout=300` is a total timeout; on requests it's per-IO. That mismatch causes confusion. We should surface that in error text. I'll add an advisory.
deploy-bot: deploy started for redwood-sdk v0.13.2 -> staging :rocket:
nitin (SDK): I'll push a patch that logs which client backend is in use and clarifies required timeout shape for long streaming gens. Also include a helper `Timeout.total()` constructor.
max (Support): For the customer: advise to explicitly set `timeout={"total":300}` or instantiate `Timeout(total=300)` and retry. Also mention HTTP_PROXY interactions and proxy idle limits.
jane (Customer): Thanks — trying `Timeout(total=300)` now.
(10m later) jane (Customer): Confirmed — streaming completes when I use the dict timeout. Thanks! :tada:
max (Support): Great. I'll update the ticket and include recommended repro steps and the SDK workaround.
nitin (SDK): Follow-up: we'll add a KB note explaining: "If you run behind a proxy or load balancer, set total deadline explicitly and ensure proxy idle timeout >= expected inter-chunk gap."
elaine (SRE): Filing an ops-runbook to check ALB timeouts for enterprise customers by default.
max (Support): Closing loop with ACME in 24h. :thumbsup:
